tests.name: accessibility + full educator-to-learner flow in the browser (axe, keyboard, labels)
startup: the documented command `npm start` serves the app
approval is enforced by the server, not just the UI
test mode records synthetic approvals as TEST approvals and labels the build
return-for-work applies the educator note as a revision and keeps history
teacher revision changes the generated experience end-to-end (prompts, criteria, runtime, feedback)
learner API never exposes prompts, engine internals or look-fors before feedback
persistence and interrupted-session recovery: a server restart resumes the exact session
concurrent learner messages are serialized without losing turns
errors are clear and do not corrupt state
trace links teacher input -> design -> evidence -> feedback, and replay verifies it
text: list splitting handles newlines, semicolons, commas and prose
text: look-for matching uses stems and requires all words of a phrase
intake: asks one question at a time, in order, and records verbatim answers
intake: too-short required answers get exactly one follow-up; required skips are challenged once
intake: template recommendation follows the described student work, and the educator can override it
intake: materials yield suggested key ideas
design: every educator answer appears in the design with educator provenance
design: missing educator input becomes visible AI assumptions, never silent
design: materials influence the design (briefing excerpts and grounding)
design: natural-language revision changes decisions and propagates to prompts, challenges and adaptation
design: unrecognized revision requests are reported, not silently ignored
design: direct edits are validated; invalid edits are refused
approval state machine: only open designs can be approved; approval needs a name; test mode yields test approval
compile: refuses an unapproved draft (approval gate)
compile: superseded cannot be approved, rejected cannot be built, approved builds a valid package
schema: validatePackage catches broken packages
runtime: phases are gated; preparation cannot be skipped and practice needs real attempts
runtime: help requests are refused with escalating cues that never reveal look-fors
runtime: adaptation events cite an approved rule and the learner turn that triggered them
runtime: feedback quotes only real learner turns, separates inference, and does not assess unseen criteria
runtime regression: refuting a misconception is not recorded as endorsing it (invented-evidence fix)
runtime: character stays consistent (same speaker; only scripted challenge lines in deterministic mode)
runtime: deterministic replay reproduces transcript, evidence and feedback
provider replacement: a model provider voices lines; leaks and errors fall back to deterministic lines
generality: two briefs from different domains produce materially different experiences with no code change
